reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is to explain how to locate Facebook support and start a Messenger conversation using the demonstrated help interface. The support availability is presented as conditional, without claiming that a representative will resolve every issue. Separate affiliate and income-related promotions, including a "$100/Day" claim, are qualified by an earnings disclaimer and are not shown to require payment, request credentials, lead to a deceptive destination, or connect to the support tutorial.

opening.argument: The description directly pairs an unusually concrete income promise with an external action: viewers are told how to build pages that make "$100/Day" and are immediately given a shortened link. It also offers a "FREE Affiliate Marketing Success Guide" through another shortened link. That is a recognizable promise-action structure: visit an external destination to pursue an easy-sounding online-income result. The support tutorial supplies a credible-looking context around these offers, but it does not establish that the linked opportunity can actually deliver the advertised outcome. The disclaimer limits guarantees, yet the promotional pairing remains explicit.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The support demonstration does not resolve the separate solicitation in the description. Showing a help interface can make the surrounding promotion appear more trustworthy, while the "$100/Day" offer and shortened link remain unexplained by the support workflow. The disclaimer also concedes that income claims are being presented; it does not verify the claim or identify what viewers receive after following the link.

opening.argument: Several concrete warning signals appear together: a "$100/Day" result, shortened external links, a free guide used to draw interest, affiliate recommendations, and repeated calls to subscribe or visit links. The offer is framed around making money online rather than a specific, verifiable service outcome. Shortened destinations conceal the final URL from the viewer in the supplied text, while the income figure is much more prominent than any explanation of the work required. Even with a disclaimer, this combination can encourage viewers to pursue a low-friction online-income path whose actual terms are not established here.

opening.argument: Although presented as operational help, the video functions within a broader promotional funnel. The description combines a Facebook-page income promise, a free affiliate-marketing guide, recommended tools, affiliate links, Instagram promotion, and a request to subscribe to weekly money-making videos. The support topic gives the presentation an authoritative business-help frame, while the surrounding calls to action steer viewers toward external offers and ongoing channel engagement. That makes the educational framing insufficient to rule out a low-barrier income solicitation.
